Nuvola icon theme 1.0 by David Vignoni, fetched 2026-09-23.
The author's page: the live domain icon-king.com is now parked (a 2017 archive
capture of the project page shows only a parking frame), so the page was read
from the Internet Archive copy of 2009-08-31:
http://web.archive.org/web/20090831103737/http://www.icon-king.com/projects/nuvola/
(saved as icon-king-nuvola-page-20090831.html). It is titled "Nuvola | David
Vignoni Visual Designer" and says the set is "a free software icon set under
the GNU LGPL 2.1", that "Version 1.0 has been released on October 15th, 2004",
and under Terms of Use "The Nuvola icons are licensed under the LGPL".
The release: nuvola-1.0.tar.gz from the Internet Archive copy of
http://www.icon-king.com/files/nuvola-1.0.tar.gz (capture 2016-03-14;
13,594,245 bytes; gzip header dated 2004-10-15): 3,706 PNG icons from 16 to
128 px, no SVG files.
Its own license files, extracted beside this file:
  license.txt  the GNU Lesser General Public License 2.1 text (26,430 bytes)
  readme.txt   "Copyright (c)  2003-2004  David Vignoni." and the LGPL notice,
               with an add-on for artwork. The add-on says: "The LGPL in some
               sections obliges you to make the files carry notices. With
               images this is in some cases impossible or hardly usefull. With
               this library a notice is placed at a prominent place in the
               directory containing the elements. You may follow this
               practice." and "The exception in section 6 of the GNU Lesser
               General Public License covers the use of elements of this art
               library in a GUI."
  author.txt   "David Vignoni (david@icon-king.com) ICON KING - www.icon-king.com"
  thanks.to    the author's thanks list
Also saved: lgpl-2.1.txt, the current text from
https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.1.txt.
What this means for the site: the folder that holds the icons on the site
carries readme.txt and license.txt beside them (the add-on's practice), and
the credits name David Vignoni.
selected-128/ holds 20 icons extracted from the 128 px folders for looking at;
any other icon can be extracted from the tarball later.
